VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | FIND: `scan_health()` also misreports tool availability on timeout/fatal execution failure, not just missing binaries. Evidence: each runner returns `[]` both when `_run_tool()` yields `stderr=="NOT_FOUND"` and when parsing fails after `TIMEOUT`, malformed output, or non-JSON stderr/stdout; `scan_health()` then sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally. FOLLOW: downstream consumers cannot distinguish “tool ran cleanly” from “tool never produced usable output”, so health scans can silently fail-open and the insect brain receives deceptively healthy infrastructure state between rounds. This broadens C0004 beyond missing binaries to all non-exception execution failures. FIX: keep C0004’s root fix but ensure runner/scan contract carries explicit execution status for success / missing / timeout / parse-failed, and set `tools_available` only for actual successful invocation.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | FIND: timeout handling is not limited to “return empty diagnostics”; it also corrupts verdict semantics in fix evaluation. Evidence: `_count_tool_issues()` treats runner timeout as zero issues because timed-out runners return `[]`; `evaluate_fix()` then computes deltas against zero and `_compute_fix_verdict()` may classify a fix as SAFE/NEUTRAL even though post-fix tool checks never completed. FOLLOW: this crosses the immune interface: Stage 4 in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE/NEUTRAL, activating the bug-closed gate in later rounds. A timed-out tool can therefore wrongly close a bug and suppress further discoveries. FIX: preserve C0021’s timeout detection, and on any timeout during baseline or post-fix checks mark the evaluation UNEVALUABLE rather than counting zero issues.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or package context; it copies only the target file to a temp directory and then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated basename file. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`, with no package tree copy, no preservation of relative path, and no sibling/module dependencies. For any fix touching a module that imports local package code, pyright/mypy/ruff behavior on the isolated file can differ materially from behavior in the real repo. This breaks the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” capability by evaluating a different program than the one actually patched.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix verdicts can become silently wrong in both directions: harmless fixes can look harmful due to unresolved local imports, and harmful fixes can look safe because repo-level interactions are absent. This directly affects `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4, which marks findings as `verified=True` on SAFE/NEUTRAL and then enables NK bug-closed suppression in later rounds. A false SAFE here can close a bug that still breaks the real codebase.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — create the sandbox by copying the full source tree needed for `source_paths` while preserving relative paths, then patch the target file at its mirrored path inside that temp tree and run tools with `cwd` set to the sandbox root against the mirrored path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` usually does not test the patched code at all. Evidence: the sandbox only contains the single patched file, but `test_cmd` is executed unchanged in `cwd=tmpdir`. In context, the immune pipeline passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; from the tempdir there is no `bench/tests/` tree, so pytest either fails immediately or, if absolute/import resolution reaches the real repo, runs against unpatched source outside the sandbox. In both cases the “sandbox-test proposed fixes” contract is violated.
FOLLOW: This invalidates the strongest downstream safety check. Fix evaluations can be marked HARMFUL for missing test paths unrelated to the patch, or SAFE/NEUTRAL without exercising the patched codepath. Because endocrine verdicts feed immune Stage 4 verification, wrong test semantics can wrongly block valid fixes or wrongly verify invalid ones, distorting later dedup/closure behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when a test command is supplied, mirror the repository subtree needed by the tests into the sandbox and rewrite any relative repo paths in `test_cmd` to the sandbox equivalents before execution.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as SAFE even when one tool category regresses, as long as another category improves more. Evidence: it sums `net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues` into `total_net`; if the sum is negative, verdict is SAFE. Example: a fix introducing one new Bandit security issue but removing two Ruff warnings yields `total_net = -1`, hence SAFE. That contradicts the documented rule “SAFE: no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: This is a silently wrong result, not mere scoring noise. A fix that introduces a new security or type error can be marked SAFE, propagated to immune Stage 4 as `verified=True`, and then used by NK as proof the bug is closed. That can suppress future findings while the codebase is objectively worse.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — declare HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; only use SAFE when at least one net field is negative and none are positive.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong file because it uses substring matching: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A short or basename-only mention in a finding/proposed fix can match multiple source paths, and the first match wins. Evidence: with similarly named paths, a fragment like `brain.py` or `bench/end` can resolve incorrectly.
FOLLOW: Wrong target resolution means the fix evaluator can modify and analyze an unrelated file while reporting against `finding.finding_id`. Downstream this yields false UNEVALUABLE/HARMFUL/SAFE judgments and can mark the wrong finding as verified in the immune pipeline, corrupting cross-round bug closure state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require exact normalized path match first, then unique basename match only; if resolution is ambiguous, return UNEVALUABLE instead of choosing the first substring hit.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `health_trend()` can return histories shorter than the number of scans even after the existing ragged-series issue is fixed for categories present intermittently, because it appends only when a category appears in a scan and never records scans with zero categories at all. Evidence: if an early scan has no diagnostics, `trend` remains empty for that round; later categories start at index 0, losing alignment with round count.
FOLLOW: Any consumer using `health_trend()` for worsening/improving detection will misalign category histories with actual rounds, producing wrong temporal inferences. This is lower impact now because the method is not wired into the brain, but it blocks the advertised trend capability from functioning correctly once connected.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — build trend arrays with one entry per scan index from `self._scan_history`, filling zero for every category on every round, including fully clean scans.
VERIFIED: TRUE
